depicts: Close, square-on photograph of the large bronze dedication tablet bolted to the riveted International Orange steel of the bridge. Four columns of raised lettering beneath a header band, flanked by two small relief panels (a landscape vignette left, a map of San Francisco Bay right). Every name is legible.
details: This is the single most important image for the credit question. The 'ENGINEERING STAFF' column reads, in order: JOSEPH B. STRAUSS, CHIEF ENGINEER / CLIFFORD E. PAINE, PRINCIPAL ASSISTANT ENGINEER / RUSSELL G. CONE, RESIDENT ENGINEER / CHARLES CLARAHAN JR., ASSISTANT ENGINEER / DWIGHT N. WETHERELL, ASSISTANT ENGINEER / O. H. AMMANN, CONSULTING ENGINEER / CHARLES DERLETH JR., CONSULTING ENGINEER / LEON S. MOISSEIFF, CONSULTING ENGINEER / SYDNEY W. TAYLOR JR., CONSULTING TRAFFIC ENGINEER / IRVING F. MORROW, CONSULTING ARCHITECT / ANDREW C. LAWSON, CONSULTING GEOLOGIST / ALLAN E. SEDGWICK, CONSULTING GEOLOGIST. Charles Alton Ellis is not on it — this is the omission itself, in bronze. Strauss appears twice: once as Chief Engineer under OFFICERS and again at the head of the engineering staff. The other columns list Officers, Directors (by county), and Contractors (Pacific Bridge Company, Bethlehem Steel, John A. Roebling's Sons Company for the cables).
visible_text: THE GOLDEN GATE BRIDGE / CONSTRUCTION BEGUN 1933 · COMPLETED 1937 · BUILT BY THE GOLDEN GATE BRIDGE AND HIGHWAY DISTRICT / INCORPORATED 1928 · COMPRISING THE COUNTIES OF SAN FRANCISCO · MARIN · NAPA · SONOMA · MENDOCINO · DEL NORTE. Column heads: OFFICERS / DIRECTORS / ENGINEERING STAFF / CONTRACTORS.
notes: Highest-resolution and most legible copy of this plaque found. A lower-resolution duplicate exists on Wikipedia (File:GoldenGate Plaque.jpg) and was rejected as a near-duplicate.

depicts: Tight vertical shot of a weathered bronze dedication tablet set into a rough concrete wall. Green-black patina with pale mineral staining; a hard diagonal shadow falls across the upper third. Deco sans-serif raised capitals.
details: The rhetoric is entirely collective and anonymous — 'those who, undaunted through the years, sought honestly and fairly through this structure to tender a definite contribution to the cultural heritage of mankind.' Not one person is named anywhere on the panel. The top edge of a second panel is visible at the bottom of the frame.
visible_text: DEDICATION BY THE DIRECTORS AND OFFICERS OF THE GOLDEN GATE BRIDGE AND HIGHWAY DISTRICT / IN THE YEAR 1937 · NINETEEN YEARS AFTER ITS INCEPTION · THE GOLDEN GATE BRIDGE OF SAN FRANCISCO IS HERE DEDICATED TO THE PEOPLE OF THE GOLDEN GATE BRIDGE AND HIGHWAY DISTRICT WHO GUARANTEED IT · TO THE CITIZENRY OF THE STATE OF CALIFORNIA WHO SPONSORED IT · AND TO THE WORLD AT LARGE WHOSE ADVENTUROUS SPIRIT IT REFLECTS ... CONCEIVED IN THE SPIRIT OF PROGRESS IT SHALL STAND AT THE GATES OF SAN FRANCISCO · A MONUMENT TO HER VISION · AN INSPIRATION TO POSTERITY ...
notes: 'Nineteen years after its inception' dates the inception to 1918-19, i.e. O'Shaughnessy's approach to Strauss.

depicts: A second bronze dedication tablet, adjacent to people-02, in the same concrete wall. Centred text with a small bear-and-flag Native Sons emblem in relief at the top. Heavy verdigris and salt bloom; a shadow of a person or post cuts in at the lower right.
details: The phrase 'engineering genius' is used in the abstract, attached to no individual. Dated MAY 27 1937, the day the bridge opened to pedestrians. Fragments of the panels above and below are visible at the frame edges.
visible_text: DEDICATION BY THE NATIVE SONS OF THE GOLDEN WEST / AS A TRIBUTE TO THE ENGINEERING GENIUS WHICH GAVE TO THE STATE OF CALIFORNIA THE GOLDEN GATE BRIDGE · THE LONGEST BRIDGE SPAN IN THE WORLD · WE · THE NATIVE SONS OF THE GOLDEN WEST · MAKE THIS DEDICATION IN RECOGNITION OF THE BEAUTY AND THE UTILITY OF THIS GREAT STRUCTURE AND THE SCIENTIFIC ACHIEVEMENT FOR WHICH IT STANDS · MAY 27 1937. Emblem lettering: N.S.G.W.

depicts: A bronze plaque mounted flat against bright orange riveted steel plate, with rows of large domed rivet heads above and below filling the top and bottom of the frame. Two circular medallions in relief at the top: left shows a tower in elevation with dates 1937 and 1962; right shows the bridge in perspective with a ship beneath.
details: The commemorative text praises 'the courageous, farsighted men who devised and built this span' — again a collective, unnamed tribute — and then names, at length, the 1962 board of directors and general manager, none of whom built anything. The contrast between the anonymous builders and the named administrators is the point. Located on the bridge's south tower, the same tower that received the Charles Ellis recognition plaque fifty years later.
visible_text: GOLDEN GATE BRIDGE 1937 1962 / 25TH ANNIVERSARY · WORLD'S GREATEST SUSPENSION BRIDGE / MAY 27, 1937 – MAY 27, 1962 / THE REDWOOD EMPIRE HONORS THE SILVER ANNIVERSARY OF THE GOLDEN GATE BRIDGE, FIRST TO LINK SAN FRANCISCO AND MARIN COUNTY; AND THE COURAGEOUS, FARSIGHTED MEN WHO DEVISED AND BUILT THIS SPAN, INDISPENSABLE FACTOR IN DEVELOPMENT OF THE VAST REDWOOD EMPIRE. / DIRECTORS, GOLDEN GATE BRIDGE & HIGHWAY DISTRICT / MATTHEW A. GRAHAM, PRESIDENT · L. E. CASTNER · PHILLIPS S. DAVIES · DANIEL F. DEL CARLO · ALVIN F. DERRE · JOSEPH J. DIVINY · HERBERT J. FEHELY · PETER A. GASSER · WILLIAM D. HADELER · BEN K. LERER · DAN E. LONDON · LELAND S. MURPHY · JOHN E. NELSON · CHARLES W. REINKING / JAMES ADAM, GENERAL MANAGER / PRESENTED BY REDWOOD EMPIRE ASSOCIATION
notes: The photograph is recent (2024) but the plaque dates from 1962.

depicts: A rough-hewn pale granite boulder in the lower left of the frame carrying a rust-coloured bronze relief plaque titled 'MEN OF VISION'. The relief shows two standing figures in suits facing each other, apparently in conversation, with a suggestion of trees or the bridge behind them. Above and right, a steep bank of ferns and spiky flowering succulents rises to the orange south tower against a clear blue sky.
details: This is the one monument on the site that is explicitly about the men rather than the structure — two figures, in conversation, cast in bronze. The plaque's body text is present but too small to read at this resolution; only the title 'MEN OF VISION' is legible. The colour is heavily saturated (scanned slide film), the greens almost fluorescent.
visible_text: MEN OF VISION (plaque title; body text present but illegible at this size).
notes: The only monument found that depicts more than one man. Useful if the narration turns on Strauss vs. the people he worked with. If the plaque's full text matters, it will need a higher-resolution source than this.

depicts: A printed invitation card on flecked cream paper. A gold-ink line engraving of the completed bridge seen from the Marin side sits at the top, above centred calligraphic text in a period Deco-inflected face. Three names with titles are printed at the bottom.
details: The document that formalises who got credit at the moment of opening. The three signatories are Angelo J. Rossi, Mayor of San Francisco; Arthur M. Brown Jr., General Chairman of the Golden Gate Bridge Fiesta; and William P. Filmer, President of the Golden Gate Bridge and Highway District. No engineer is named — not Strauss, not Ellis, not Moisseiff, not Morrow. The paper's flecks and the gold ink read clearly at full size.
visible_text: The Citizens of San Francisco and the Redwood Empire Counties of California request the honor of your presence to witness the ceremonies at the opening of the Golden Gate Bridge and the attendant Fiesta / San Francisco, May twenty-seventh to June second, Nineteen hundred and thirty-seven / Angelo J. Rossi, Mayor of San Francisco / Arthur M. Brown, Jr., General Chairman, Golden Gate Bridge Fiesta / William P. Filmer, President, Golden Gate Bridge and Highway District
notes: Arthur M. Brown Jr. also appears as a San Francisco director on the bridge's own dedication tablet (people-01).

attribution: Internet Archive Book Images, from The Architect and Engineer, August 1933
depicts: Halftone photograph, printed in a 1933 trade journal, of four men standing on bare dirt at the left of a very large fresh concrete block with faceted, stepped sides. Left to right: a stocky bald man in a dark three-piece suit holding a hat; a younger man in a suit and tie, partly hidden behind him; a tall man in a field jacket, breeches and laced knee-boots; and a tall, wavy-haired man in a loose suit standing with his hands behind his back. Three more men in hats stand on top of the block against the sky, with two others near a ladder propped against the far edge.
details: The magazine's caption names them: 'COMPLETED MARIN PIER, GOLDEN GATE BRIDGE. 24,000 cubic yards of concrete required. Cost of pier $405,000. Reading from left to right — James Reed, General Manager; C. F. Paine, Principal Assistant Chief Engineer of Strauss Corp.; James Graham and Russell G. Cone, Resident Engineer of the Strauss Corporation.' This is a named photograph of the Golden Gate Bridge engineering staff at work in 1933. Paine and Cone both appear on the bridge's dedication tablet (people-01). The scale is legible from the men: the pier face towers over them. The men on top give the height a second reading. Boot-and-breeches versus city suit distinguishes the field engineers from the office.
visible_text: Printed below the image: "Golden Gate" Cement used.
notes: Strong candidate for any line about the men around Strauss. Note Clifford E. Paine — the man Strauss promoted to Principal Assistant Engineer at roughly the moment he dismissed Ellis. Halftone screen is visible at full size.

attribution: Internet Archive Book Images, from The Architect and Engineer, 1933
depicts: A soft pencil-and-wash elevation drawing, reproduced in halftone, of a proposed Golden Gate crossing. At the left a heavy braced cantilever arch springs from the San Francisco shore; from the arch's far pier a stiffening truss runs level to a slender tower at right, which carries a suspension cable. Flat grey water fills the bottom third; the sky is blank paper.
details: A hybrid: cantilever at one end, suspension at the other. The tower is a plain latticed post with none of the stepped Art Deco fluting of the bridge as built. This is the visual evidence of Strauss the drawbridge and cantilever man before the suspension design was worked out by others. A small ink blot sits in the sky at upper centre.
visible_text: None legible.
notes: Pairs with people-09, a wider rendering of the same hybrid scheme. Useful for the 'this was his first suspension bridge' line.

attribution: Internet Archive Book Images, from The Architect and Engineer, 1933
depicts: A wider version of the same hybrid-scheme rendering: a trestle viaduct runs down a headland at the far left, then a braced cantilever arch over the shore, then a level truss deck running right to a tower carrying suspension cables. Grey water below, empty pale sky above with soft charcoal shading in the upper left.
details: Shows more of the approach structure than people-08 — you can follow the road from the hillside all the way out over the water. A pencilled signature and date sit in the lower left corner of the drawing, too fine to read at this resolution. A speck of ink floats mid-sky.
visible_text: Illegible pencil signature and date, lower left of the drawing.
notes: Near-relative of people-08 but a different crop/drawing with more approach context; kept both.

attribution: Unidentified photographer; M. M. O'Shaughnessy photograph collection, Bancroft Library (via Calisphere)
depicts: Sepia-toned studio head-and-shoulders portrait of an elderly white man in three-quarter view, body turned to the viewer's right, eyes toward the camera. High balding forehead, white hair swept back at the sides, heavy white eyebrows, full white walrus moustache. He wears a dark pinstriped three-piece suit with a wing-collar shirt and a dark spotted cravat. The background is a soft dark studio wash; the print has the creamy, slightly out-of-focus quality of a 1910s-20s portrait.
details: Michael Maurice O'Shaughnessy, San Francisco's City Engineer — the man who wrote to bridge engineers around 1919 asking whether a Golden Gate crossing was possible, and who brought Strauss in. Expression is level and unsmiling; the lighting is soft from the upper left. Verified identity from the Bancroft Library collection metadata.
visible_text: None.
notes: One of only two authenticated period portraits of a named participant found in free sources (the other is Giannini, people-11). No free portrait of Strauss, Ellis, Moisseiff or Morrow could be located.

attribution: Agence Rol (press photograph), Bibliothèque nationale de France / Gallica
depicts: Black-and-white press photograph, head and shoulders, of a middle-aged white man photographed outdoors against a plain pale wall. He wears a light snap-brim fedora tilted back, a dark pinstriped suit, a stiff white wing collar and a heavy knitted tie. Dark hair greying at the temples, thick dark moustache, deep-set eyes looking off to the viewer's right and slightly up.
details: Amadeo Pietro Giannini of the Bank of Italy (later Bank of America), the banker who bought the first Golden Gate Bridge bonds in 1932 when nobody else would. A small round lapel pin is visible. The negative has scattered white dust specks and a light fogged patch across the lower left. A single thin wire crosses the sky at upper left. Photographed in March 1927, five years before the bond purchase.
visible_text: None.
notes: French press-agency caption identifies him as 'M. A. P. Giannini, président de la Banque d'Italie [à San Francisco]'. Identity is secure.

attribution: Irving Underhill, Library of Congress Prints and Photographs Division
depicts: Elevated black-and-white view over Lower Manhattan rooftops toward the Manhattan Bridge under construction across the East River. The near tower rises at right, its deck level only partly built out — cranes and derricks sit on the exposed steel, with open air where the roadway will be. The far tower stands complete at left. The main cables sweep between them with the vertical suspender ropes already hung but nothing yet suspended from most of them. Tugs, barges and a ferry work the river; the 'CATHARINE FERRY' terminal, coal and lumber yards, and tenement rooftops fill the foreground.
details: Leon Moisseiff's bridge, and his credential. This is a deflection-theory suspension bridge caught mid-erection: the cable geometry is finished and the deck is being hung from it, exactly the sequence the Golden Gate would follow twenty-seven years later. A faint typed caption is printed into the sky at centre. Signs read 'CARSTEN...', 'MOQUIN OFFERMAN', 'LUMBER', and a building date '1895' on a cornice at lower right. A horse-drawn wagon stands in the ferry approach.
visible_text: Faint caption block in the sky, centre: 'MANHATTAN BRIDGE ... [made] March 23rd 1909 ... Irving Underhill, 18 Park Place, N.Y.' Signage in the scene: CATHARINE FERRY; LUMBER; MOQUIN OFFERMAN.
notes: Moisseiff was the Manhattan Bridge's designer; this is the work that made him the suspension authority Strauss had to hire.

attribution: Bain News Service, via Library of Congress (Flickr Commons)
depicts: Black-and-white glass-plate view down a wide unpaved street toward the Manhattan Bridge's monumental Beaux-Arts entrance: a triumphal arch flanked by curving colonnades. Through the arch, one of the bridge's steel towers is visible in the distance. In the foreground a dozen or more workmen in shirtsleeves, caps and hats dig, shovel and push a wheelbarrow; broken paving stones are heaped in a mound at right. An early open-cab motor truck and a horse cart stand mid-ground. Shopfronts at left advertise WATCHES JEWELRY.
details: The frame contains both registers of a bridge project: the ceremonial architecture at the far end and the men with shovels in the dirt at the near end. The plate is hand-titled in grease pencil at the top. Two men in white shirts and straw boaters walk down the centre of the street, dressed unlike the labourers around them.
visible_text: Hand-lettered on the negative: 'MANHATTAN BRIDGE' (upper left) and '3934-2' (upper right). Shop signage: WATCHES JEWELRY.
notes: Moisseiff's bridge again, in the years just after completion. Bain News Service negative held by the Library of Congress.

attribution: Bain News Service, via Library of Congress (Flickr Commons)
depicts: Companion plate to people-13, taken from a higher and more oblique angle. The Manhattan Bridge arch and colonnade fill the centre; the bridge's steel tower and cables are visible at the right edge beyond the plaza. In the foreground, a construction yard: long steel beams and timbers stacked in the dirt, a covered work shed with a parasol, a police call box, and streetcar tracks curving away at left. Pedestrians in long coats and hats cross the plaza. A horse-drawn van and a boxy motor car sit at far left in front of tall apartment blocks.
details: A telegraph or trolley wire cuts diagonally across the upper right of the frame. The plaza is finished and formal while the ground in front of it is still a materials dump — the same seam between the ceremonial and the working parts of a bridge as people-13. A church spire and a taller commercial tower rise on the left skyline.
visible_text: Hand-lettered on the negative: 'MANHATTAN BRIDGE' (upper left) and '3934-1' (upper right).
notes: Sequential negative number to people-13; same session.

depicts: A large monochrome architectural rendering in grey wash and gouache, aged to warm sepia at the edges, giving a bird's-eye view of the Brooklyn plaza of the Manhattan Bridge. The elevated approach roadway and railway run away from the viewer toward a distant tower; below, a formal plaza with two ornate monuments, allotments of trees, tramcars, early automobiles, horse carts and scores of tiny drawn pedestrians. Street names are lettered onto the drawing. Factory chimneys smoke on the horizon; another suspension bridge is drawn faintly at the far right.
details: An idealised, populated vision of what a bridge approach was supposed to become — the promotional register Strauss worked in for a decade. Streets labelled SANDS ST., HIGH ST., NASSAU ST., BRIDGE ST., JAY ST., PEARL ST. The artist's signature 'H. M. Pettit' is in the lower left corner. The paper is scorched or foxed along the top and right edges.
visible_text: Street labels lettered on the drawing: SANDS ST., HIGH ST., NASSAU ST., BRIDGE ST., JAY ST., PEARL ST. Signed lower left: H. M. Pettit.
notes: Peripheral to the credit story; included as Moisseiff-adjacent material and as an example of period bridge promotion art.

depicts: Modern colour photograph, very wide and shallow, looking down on the East River from a high vantage in winter. The pale blue Manhattan Bridge crosses the centre of the frame with both towers and the full main span visible; the stone tower and cables of the Brooklyn Bridge cut into the lower right corner. Snow lies on the rooftops of Brooklyn and on the Manhattan waterfront at left; a tug pushes upriver mid-frame. Grey overcast light, no shadows.
details: Shows the bridge Moisseiff actually designed as it stands: a stiffening truss of shallow depth carried on a long, flat cable sag — the deflection-theory profile. Both East River bridges in one frame lets the older, heavier Brooklyn Bridge sit next to the lighter Manhattan Bridge for comparison. Industrial chimneys, a red ship at the Manhattan pier, and a 'SELF STORAGE' billboard on the Brooklyn side.
visible_text: A billboard on the Brooklyn shore reads SELF STORAGE with a phone number, illegible at this size.
notes: Extreme aspect ratio (2.26:1) — will letterbox or need cropping against a 16:9 deck.

depicts: The bronze Joseph B. Strauss statue on its cylindrical concrete pedestal, seen from slightly below and to the left against a clear deep-blue sky. The figure stands in a three-piece suit, feet apart, left hand at his side holding what appears to be a small object, right arm holding a rolled drawing tucked under the arm. Behind and to the left, the Golden Gate Bridge's south tower and cables rise in International Orange with the Marin headlands beyond. Clipped hedge, flowerbeds and a cypress fill the middle ground.
details: A small child in dark clothing is crouched at the base of the pedestal at lower left, reading something — giving the scale of the eight-foot figure. The sculptor's incised signature and the date 1941 are legible on the plinth beneath the feet. The bronze dedication plaque on the pedestal face reads at the top '1870 JOSEPH B. STRAUSS 1938' and beneath it '"THE MAN WHO BUILT THE BRIDGE"'; the rest is legible only in outline.
visible_text: On the plinth: 1941 / Frederick W. Schweigardt. On the pedestal plaque: 1870 JOSEPH B. STRAUSS 1938 / "THE MAN WHO BUILT THE BRIDGE" / (further lines about the bridge and the statue, faint).
notes: The phrase 'THE MAN WHO BUILT THE BRIDGE' cast in bronze is the single sharpest artefact of the credit problem. Statue commissioned by the District; Strauss's widow funded the memorial; dedicated 1941, three years after his death.

depicts: The Strauss statue filling almost the whole tall frame, shot from below against clear blue sky, cropped at the ankles. The modelling of the face is clear: heavy brows drawn together, downturned mouth, hair swept back. Three-piece suit with a buttoned waistcoat, jacket open; left hand at his side, right forearm clamping a rolled drawing whose scrolled ends are distinct. Behind at left, the orange cables and deck of the bridge with green Marin hills; at right, a dark cypress and flowering shrubs.
details: The best available reading of the sculpted face and of the rolled plans under his arm — the sculptor's shorthand for 'this man designed it', which is exactly the claim in dispute. The incised signature '1941 / Frederick W. Schweigardt' is legible on the plinth at the bottom edge of the frame. Bronze has gone green-grey in the recesses and warm brown on the raised surfaces.
visible_text: On the plinth, lower edge: 1941 / Frederick W. Schweigardt.
notes: Tallest and most detailed of the statue images (2:3 portrait, 2883px). Good for a slow push on the face.

depicts: The Strauss statue on its pedestal under flat white overcast, shot straight on from a low path. The bronze is dark and cool; the pedestal plaque is a small green rectangle, unreadable. Behind at left the orange south tower stands against featureless white sky; conifers and clipped hedge fill the right half. Two hikers with a red backpack stand on the path at far left.
details: The un-flattering, overcast version — no sky, no drama, the statue reduced to a dark figure on a concrete drum in a municipal garden. Early digital capture (2002) so the resolution is modest and colours are muted. The pre-2012 setting: plain paving and a simple concrete base, before the Legacy Circle plaza was built around it.
visible_text: None legible.
notes: Documents the site as it looked before the 2012 Joseph Strauss Legacy Circle reconstruction — the other statue images mostly post-date that change.

attribution: Carol M. Highsmith, Library of Congress (Jon B. Lovelace Collection of California Photographs)
depicts: Formal frontal record photograph of the Strauss statue centred on its wide circular concrete plinth, on a large empty pale-paved plaza under a clear blue sky. Behind, a planted bank of aeoniums, yellow and purple flowering shrubs; at upper right the orange south tower and cables. At upper left, a viewing terrace with red railings, an interpretive banner with a historic photograph, and a lone visitor.
details: The plinth's outer band carries printed text: 'JOSEPH STRAUSS LEGACY CIRCLE' across the front, with '75TH ANNIVERSARY SPONSORS' and a donor list (Odwalla, Chevron, Hanson Bridgett LLP, Levi Strauss & Co., Pacific Gas and Electric Company, Speck Products) to the left, and 'STRAUSS CIRCLE LEAD GIFT — INDIVIDUAL GIFT: Lisa and Douglas Goldman Fund; CORPORATE GIFT: Bank of America' to the right, plus the URL www.goldengatebridge75.org. The small bronze 1941 plaque is still on the plinth top, and a round metal time-capsule or light fitting is set into the paving beside it.
visible_text: JOSEPH STRAUSS LEGACY CIRCLE / Take your place in the Strauss Circle and support the Golden Gate Bridge's legacy for generations to come. / www.goldengatebridge75.org / 75TH ANNIVERSARY SPONSORS: Odwalla, Chevron, Hanson Bridgett LLP, Levi Strauss & Co., Pacific Gas and Electric Company, Speck Products / STRAUSS CIRCLE LEAD GIFT — INDIVIDUAL GIFT: Lisa and Douglas Goldman Fund; CORPORATE GIFT: Bank of America
notes: Public domain and cleanly lit, so the safest hero shot of the statue. Bank of America's name on the plinth ties back to Giannini (people-11). Shot in January 2012, months before the 75th anniversary.

depicts: Wide 3:2 landscape from the Strauss Circle plaza: an expanse of empty pale paving fills the bottom third, the small dark Strauss statue stands on its plinth at the far left edge, and the Golden Gate Bridge occupies the rest of the frame — south tower, full main span, north tower, sweeping cables, all in International Orange against a cloudless blue sky, with the tawny Marin headlands behind. A flowering red bottlebrush and a cypress frame the right side; a scattering of visitors stands at a railing in the middle distance.
details: The only image in this set that gives both the man and the whole bridge in one 16:9-friendly frame, with the statue tiny and the structure enormous — a ready-made visual argument about scale of credit versus scale of object. The 'JOSEPH STRAUSS LEGACY CIRCLE' band on the plinth is visible but too small to read. Another small memorial stone (probably the 'Men of Vision' boulder, people-05) is visible in the mid-right foliage.
visible_text: Plinth band lettering visible but illegible at this size.
notes: Best landscape composition for a 16:9 deck; most of the other statue images are portrait.

depicts: Near-16:9 landscape, low three-quarter view of the Strauss statue from its right side, the figure filling the centre and cropped at the shins by the bottom of the frame. Broken cloud over a bright grey-white sky. Behind at left, the top of the bridge's south tower rises above a bank of aeoniums and iceplant; a utility pole and cypresses at right; the pale paving and grey kerbing of the new plaza in the lower foreground.
details: The three-quarter angle reads the pose differently from the frontal shots — the rolled drawing under the right arm is silhouetted clear of the body, and the set of the jaw is more pronounced. A red-orange digital date stamp is burned into the lower right corner. Shot two months after the 75th anniversary and the Legacy Circle's dedication.
visible_text: Camera date stamp burned into lower right: 2012-07-17 11:30:56
notes: The burned-in timestamp is intrusive but confirms the date; it sits in dead space at the lower right and could be cropped.

depicts: Twilight 16:9 landscape. The Strauss statue stands almost dead centre on the illuminated circular plinth, lit from below by a single ground-set uplight that throws hard shadows up under the brow and chin. Behind, a black mass of hillside planting silhouetted against a sky graded from dusty blue at the top to peach at the horizon. The plaza paving and a low retaining wall run across the lower third, catching a line of warm light. Water and a distant headland are just visible at the right edge.
details: The uplighting turns the face into a mask — deep shadow in the eye sockets, the mouth a dark line. The plinth's outer band is legible in the foreground: 'JOSEPH STRAUSS LEGACY CIRCLE / THE STRAUSS CIRCLE COMMEMORATES THE 75TH ANNIVERSARY ... AND HONORS THE LEGACY OF JOSEPH B. STRAUSS, ITS FIRST CHIEF ENGINEER / MAY 27, 2012', with a 'SPONSORS' list running away to the left. Several lens-flare orbs float in the frame.
visible_text: JOSEPH STRAUSS LEGACY CIRCLE / THE STRAUSS CIRCLE COMMEMORATES THE 75TH ANNIVERSARY [OF THE GOLDEN GATE BRIDGE] AND HONORS THE LEGACY OF JOSEPH B. STRAUSS, ITS FIRST CHIEF ENGINEER / MAY 27, 2012 / SPONSORS ...
notes: Note the careful 2012 wording, 'its first chief engineer' — a hedge the 1941 plaque's 'the man who built the bridge' does not make. A near-duplicate frame from the same shoot was rejected.

depicts: Night photograph, close on the Strauss statue from the waist up, filling the left two-thirds of the frame. The bronze is lit warm gold from below; the face is turned up and slightly right, brows knotted, mouth set hard, eyes in deep shadow. Behind, a deep navy sky with visible stars, and at lower right the bridge's south tower glowing orange under its own floodlights, with red aircraft-warning lights on the tower and along the cable.
details: The most dramatic and least documentary of the statue images — the figure reads as monumental and slightly grim, the bridge reduced to a distant glow behind him. Shot on a new moon, hence the stars. Every button on the waistcoat is picked out by the raking light.
visible_text: Photographer's circular watermark, upper right: DENNIS STANWORTH / www.dennisstanworth.com
notes: Watermarked and All Rights Reserved on Flickr. Kept because the composition is unlike anything else in the set; check licensing before any use beyond personal viewing.

depicts: Telephoto portrait-format shot: the Strauss statue from the knees up, sharply lit and warm gold-brown, set against the out-of-focus orange south tower which fills the whole background with its stacked rectangular portals and vertical cable curtain. Deep blue sky above, hazy Marin hills at lower left, dark shrubbery across the bottom.
details: The long lens flattens the space so the tower sits directly behind his head like a backdrop, the figure and the structure locked in one plane. The rolled drawing under the right arm is clearly modelled with scrolled ends. Saturated, slightly grainy scanned-slide colour.
visible_text: None.

depicts: Steep low-angle close-up of the Strauss statue against unbroken deep blue sky — nothing else in the frame. The figure is cropped at the thighs, seen from below and slightly left, the head thrown back against the sky. Strong sunlight makes the bronze glow gold-orange along the shoulders, lapels and the rolled drawing, with cooler brown-green in the shadows.
details: The most heroic framing available: no bridge, no plaza, no plinth text, just the man and the sky. The waistcoat buttons, the knotted tie, the cuff of the jacket sleeve and the scrolled ends of the drawing are all crisply modelled. Useful precisely because it presents the myth uncritically and can be undercut by narration.
visible_text: None.

depicts: Portrait-format shot with the Strauss statue small in the lower left quarter, cropped at the hips by the shrubbery, and the bridge's south tower rising huge through the rest of the frame — full tower, all portals, the main cable and the suspender curtain sweeping down to the deck, the Marin headlands and a wisp of the north approach behind. Saturated blue sky.
details: The clearest statement of proportion in the set: the memorialised man occupies a corner, the object occupies everything else. The deck's stiffening truss, lamp standards and the road railing are legible below the tower. Scanned-slide colour, warm and slightly grainy.
visible_text: None.
notes: Good counterpart to people-26 (which does the opposite — man only, no bridge).

depicts: The Strauss statue on its pre-2012 plain concrete drum pedestal, three-quarter view from the left, against blue sky with high white cloud. Behind at left, the bridge's south tower and main span; behind at right, dark hedge, a cypress, and a bed of yellow daffodils in bloom. A man and a woman in dark jackets walk away along the path at the left of the frame, backs to the camera.
details: The two walkers give scale and make the point that the memorial is a thing people walk past. The bronze plaque on the pedestal face is legible as a shape with the header line '1870 JOSEPH B. STRAUSS 1938' just readable. Sharp, even late-afternoon light; the sculptor's incised name is visible on the plinth beneath the shoes.
visible_text: Pedestal plaque header, faint: 1870 JOSEPH B. STRAUSS 1938. Incised on the plinth: Frederick W. Schweigardt.
notes: All Rights Reserved on Flickr. The photographer's caption confirms the sculptor as Frederick William Schweigardt (1885-1948) and the statue's commission by the District.

depicts: Wide 4:3 view of the memorial in its garden setting under broken cloud. The Strauss statue stands on its concrete drum right of centre on a circular paved apron; the bridge's south tower and main span rise behind at right. Four visitors are in frame: an elderly woman in a pink sun hat with a shopping bag at far left, a woman in a red dress on the path, and a couple standing at the plinth looking up at the statue. Beds of yellow, purple and white bedding plants, clipped hedges and cypresses fill the middle ground.
details: The best image of the memorial as a functioning tourist stop rather than an icon — people arriving, looking, drifting past. A second, smaller memorial stone (a pale boulder with a dark plaque, almost certainly the 'Men of Vision' marker of people-05) stands on the grass at left. The pedestal plaque is a small dark rectangle, not readable.
visible_text: Photographer's script watermark, lower right: © Peter Beljaards
notes: Watermarked and All Rights Reserved on Flickr. The pre-2012 style plain drum plinth appears here in 2022, suggesting the older base was retained inside the Legacy Circle apron.

depicts: Near-16:9 landscape of the Joseph Strauss Legacy Circle under flat white summer overcast, no bridge visible. The statue stands centre on its wide low circular plinth on an expanse of tan paving. Behind, a steep bank of aeoniums, agaves and flowering shrubs; at upper left, a US flag on a tall pole, a viewing terrace with red railings, and a row of red-framed interpretive panels. Four visitors stand near the terrace, two of them with wheeled airport-style luggage carts.
details: The plinth's front band reads clearly: 'JOSEPH STRAUSS LEGACY CIRCLE / THE STRAUSS CIRCLE COMMEMORATES THE 75TH ANNIVERSARY OF THE GOLDEN GATE BRIDGE AND HONORS THE LEGACY OF JOSEPH B. STRAUSS, ITS FIRST CHIEF ENGINEER / MAY 27, 2012', with 'ANNIVERSARY SPONSORS' at the left end and 'STRAUSS CIRCLE LEAD GIFT' at the right. Grey, shadowless fog light — the bridge is completely absent from the frame, so the memorial stands alone.
visible_text: JOSEPH STRAUSS LEGACY CIRCLE / THE STRAUSS CIRCLE COMMEMORATES THE 75TH ANNIVERSARY OF THE GOLDEN GATE BRIDGE AND HONORS THE LEGACY OF JOSEPH B. STRAUSS, ITS FIRST CHIEF ENGINEER / MAY 27, 2012
notes: All Rights Reserved on Flickr. Landscape orientation and readable 2012 dedication text make this a strong pairing for any line about the District's later re-framing of Strauss.

depicts: The Strauss statue three-quarters on from the left, on the Legacy Circle plinth, under a hard blue midday sky. The upper part of the bridge's south tower shows small and orange over the planted bank behind. The plinth's front and left faces are turned toward the camera and their engraved text fills the lower quarter of the frame.
details: The best legible reading of the plinth's donor band anywhere in the set: '75TH ANNIVERSARY SPONSORS — Genentech, Hewlett-Packard, Odwalla, Chevron, Hanson Bridgett LLP, Kaiser Permanente, Wells Fargo, Levi Strauss & Co., Pacific Gas and Electric Company, Speck Products' on the left face, and 'JOSEPH STRAUSS LEGACY CIRCLE / THE STRAUSS CIRCLE COMMEMORATES THE 75TH ANNIVERSARY OF THE GOLDEN GATE BRIDGE AND HONORS THE LEGACY OF JOSEPH B. STRAUSS, ITS FIRST CHIEF ENGINEER / MAY 27, 2012' across the front. The small 1941 bronze plaque and a round blue-glass time-capsule cover are set into the plinth top beside his feet. A small grey light fitting sits on the retaining wall behind.

STRAUSS, ITS FIRST CHIEF ENGINEER / MAY 27, 2012
notes: Freely licensed (CC BY) and the corporate sponsor list is fully readable — the modern commercial afterlife of the credit.

depicts: The Strauss statue on its plain concrete drum, three-quarter view from the left, against clear blue sky — no bridge in frame at all. Behind, dark cypress and pine, a low flowering hedge and a long bed of mixed bedding flowers in red, yellow and white, with mown lawn and pale paving in the foreground.
details: Without the bridge for context this reads as a generic municipal statue of an unremarkable man in a suit in a park — which is arguably the point about how thin the public memory of these people is. The pedestal's small bronze plaque is a clear rectangle, with the header line '1870 JOSEPH B. STRAUSS 1938' just discernible. Clean shadowless light on the bronze.
visible_text: Pedestal plaque, faint: 1870 JOSEPH B. STRAUSS 1938 (remaining lines illegible).
notes: The photographer's caption confirms the memorial was executed by sculptor Frederick William Schweigardt in 1941 on commission from the Golden Gate Bridge and Highway District, and that the bronze figure is eight feet tall.
